title: CrimeNER: Curated Dataset and Methods for Research and Investigation in Language Intelligence
abstract: arXiv:2603.02150v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: The extraction of critical information from crime-related documents is a crucial task for law enforcement agencies. The extraction of this information can be interpreted as a Named-Entity Recognition (NER) task. However, there is a considerable lack of adequately annotated data on general real-world crime scenarios. To address this issue, we present CrimeNER, a case study of crime-related NER, and a general crime-related Named-Entity Recognition database (CrimeNER-db), consisting of more than 1.5K annotated documents extracted from public reports of terrorist attacks and the US Department of Justice's press notes. We define 4 coarse types of crime entity and 21 fine-grained entity types. We address the quality of the presented database with fully supervised experiments using flat and nested NER architectures and zero- and few-shot experiments using Large Language Models (LLMs). The database is available on GitHub.

translated_title: CrimeNER：用于语言智能研究与调查的精选数据集与方法
translated_abstract: 从犯罪相关文档中提取关键信息是执法机构的一项重要任务。这种信息的提取可以被理解为命名实体识别（NER）任务。然而，关于一般真实世界犯罪场景的充分标注数据相当匮乏。为解决这一问题，我们提出了CrimeNER，这是一项犯罪相关NER的案例研究，同时构建了一个通用的犯罪相关命名实体识别数据库，该数据库由从恐怖袭击公开报告和美国司法部新闻稿中提取的超过1500份标注文档组成。我们定义了4种粗粒度犯罪实体类型和21种细粒度实体类型。我们通过使用扁平与嵌套NER架构的全监督实验，以及使用大语言模型（LLMs）的零样本和少样本实验，验证了该数据库的质量。该数据库已在GitHub上公开提供。
tldr: 该论文提出了CrimeNER，一个包含1500多份标注文档的犯罪领域命名实体识别数据集，定义了4种粗粒度和21种细粒度犯罪实体类型，并通过传统NER模型和大语言模型的实验验证了数据集质量。
